claims.text: Controlled thermomechanical processing can produce an ultrafine duplex microstructure in a high-entropy alloy.
The targeted duplex microstructure comprises refined grains or grain boundaries and a distributed secondary phase.
An ultrafine duplex microstructure improves strength relative to conventional processing.
An ultrafine duplex microstructure improves ductility relative to conventional processing.
An ultrafine duplex microstructure improves Young's modulus relative to conventional processing.
An ultrafine duplex microstructure improves fracture resistance relative to conventional processing.
The refined duplex microstructure controls dislocation mobility.
Refined grain boundaries provide additional grain-boundary strengthening.
Dislocation-mobility control and grain-boundary strengthening jointly produce balanced gains in yield strength, ductility, modulus, and fracture resistance.
The improvements in the four mechanical properties will be synergistic rather than confined to individual properties.
Avoiding excessive grain growth and obtaining the duplex structure require tightly controlled temperature, strain, and cooling conditions.
The intervention is expected to work only for compositions capable of forming both a fine-grained matrix and a secondary phase.
Grain-coarsening temperatures or competing phase transformations can prevent the proposed improvements.
Success is operationally associated with at least a 10% improvement in at least three of the four key mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis is contingent on actually achieving the ultrafine duplex microstructure, but the falsification rule treats failure to produce that microstructure as falsification. Failure to implement the intended mediator does not decisively test the conditional causal hypothesis.

The hypothesis predicts improvement in all four properties, whereas the rule uses a threshold involving only at least three properties. It therefore permits one claimed property to fail without clearly determining whether the all-four-property hypothesis is falsified.
